newsitem.title: USA: Bradley buys four malls for $25 million.
newsitem.headline: Bradley buys four malls for $25 million.

text.p: Bradley Real Estate Inc said Thursday it acquired four Midwest shopping centers in the past month for a total of about $25 million.
The acquisitions include the Martin's Bittersweet Plaza, a 78,000 square foot, 98 percent-occupied center in Mishawaka, Ind., the real estate investment trust said.

Also acquired was Santa Fe Square, a 134,000 square foot, 94 percent-occupied center in Olathe, Kan.; Warren Plaza, a 90,000 square foot, 100 percent-occupied center in Dubuque, Iowa; and Roseville Center, a 77,000 square foot, 94 percent-occupied center located in Roseville, Minn.

"These acquisitions reflect Bradley's focus on grocery-anchored neighborhood and community shopping centers located in both the primary and secondary markets in the Midwest," Bradley chief executive officer Tom D'Arcy said in a news release.
